source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
The source presentation includes a side-by-side comparison table contrasting conventional/traditional rice practice (តាមទំលាប់) against SRI practice (តាម ប.វ.ស):

Seed and nursery: Traditional - seed is not selected for purity or full/plump grains; nursery beds are kept with a lot of standing water and seed is sown thickly/densely. SRI - pure, plump seed is selected before sowing; the nursery bed is a well-drained upland-style bed and seed is sown thinly.

Transplanting age and method: Traditional - seedlings are pulled and transplanted mixed together without sorting, often with weak/soft stems; seedlings are old, one month or more in age; pulled seedlings are tied into bundles and left sitting for 1-2 nights before transplanting; hills are spaced unevenly with no clear row pattern. SRI - only healthy, separated seedlings are taken for transplanting, 1-2 seedlings per hill (with best practice being a single seedling); seedlings are young, less than 15 days old; seedlings are pulled fresh and transplanted immediately after pulling; hills are planted in straight, evenly spaced rows.

Water management: Traditional - water is kept standing in the field continuously throughout the crop's growth. SRI - water is kept shallow/minimal, ideally just enough to keep the soil moist.

Weeding: Traditional - weeding is not done on time and not frequent. SRI - weeding is done frequently and on schedule/regularly.

Fertilizer: Traditional - decomposed organic waste/compost is not used as natural fertilizer; only chemical fertilizer is relied on. SRI - natural fertilizer is used, including upland-style compost and "water compost" (organic matter decomposed with water), which is incorporated into the soil.

Seed saving: Traditional - seed for the next planting is not specifically set aside/selected before harvest. SRI - seed selection and setting-aside for the next season is done before harvest, and the seed is properly stored/preserved.
